name: Small RSC Case
note: Illustrative example case size, not an industry standard — CapePack's Stock Cases database is meant to hold YOUR company's actual case inventory. Weight is empty-case (tare) weight; maxWeight is a rough carrying-capacity ceiling. Length/Width/Height are OUTSIDE dimensions; wallThickness (~3mm, typical single-wall corrugated caliper) is subtracted ×2 per axis to get the inside fit dimensions. (Migrated to the real ID/OD schema — see Databases > Cases and Trays.)

name: Medium RSC Case
note: Illustrative example only — same caveat as the small case. (Migrated to the real ID/OD schema — see Databases > Cases and Trays.)

name: Large RSC Case
note: Illustrative example only — same caveat as the small case. Slightly thicker wall than the smaller cases, as larger RSCs typically use a heavier board grade. (Migrated to the real ID/OD schema — see Databases > Cases and Trays.)

name: Euro Container Module (600x400mm)
note: 600x400mm is the real, standardized European transport-packaging module footprint ("Eurobox"), used throughout EU logistics as a base unit that divides evenly across EUR-pallet footprints. Height/weight/wallThickness here are a typical example (these are usually injection-molded plastic containers, ~2-3mm wall), not part of the standard itself. (Migrated to the real ID/OD schema — see Databases > Cases and Trays.)

name: Euro Container Module (400x300mm)
note: 400x300mm is the half-module size of the standardized European Eurobox footprint (two fit inside one 600x400mm module). Height/weight/wallThickness here are a typical example, not part of the standard itself. (Migrated to the real ID/OD schema — see Databases > Cases and Trays.)
